request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Patient name]

DOB: [Patient date of birth]

Medical Record Number: [Patient's medical record number]

Admission Date: [Date of admission]

Discharge Date: [Date of discharge]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and was diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy in the right adnexa. A laparoscopic right salpingectomy was performed, and regular obstetric follow-up was done for the intrauterine pregnancy. The baby was delivered via spontaneous vaginal delivery at term with no significant complications.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to continue with regular obstetric follow-up and to report any signs of complications immediately. Post-operative pain management should be done as prescribed. The patient should have a healthy diet and stay hydrated, and avoid strenuous physical activity until cleared by the obstetrician. 

Follow-up:

The patient is advised to schedule a follow-up appointment with their obstetrician as soon as possible.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The summary describes an ectopic pregnancy in the right adnexa, treated with laparoscopic salpingectomy. It also mentions a concurrent intrauterine pregnancy that was followed and delivered at term, which suggests a heterotopic pregnancy.

The episode being coded is the admission for abdominal pain, where the ectopic pregnancy was diagnosed and surgically treated. That makes the ectopic pregnancy the condition chiefly responsible for the care, even though the delivery is also described.

In ICD-10, ectopic pregnancy is coded to O00 (O00.0 abdominal, O00.1 tubal, O00.8 other, O00.9 unspecified). A tubal pregnancy treated with salpingectomy would be O00.1. The adnexal location fits a tubal pregnancy, and the salpingectomy supports it. Heterotopic pregnancy is also indexed under O00.8, but the principal diagnosis here is still within O00.

CODE: O00
